title: Compliance requirements catalog
description: The requirements catalog, as defined in The Software Field Guide, issue #107: the compliance-as-code chapter's companion YAML — the requirements the estate must satisfy, as data. The catalog is the join document of the compliance controls-as-data gate (policies/compliance): every requirement id declared here must have a control mapped onto it in the controls manifest (examples/compliance/controls.yaml), and a control mapping onto an id the catalog never declared is refused. This schema mirrors the shape rules of the Rego validator's gate-side catalog findings; the gate reads what the join needs — the requirement ids — while the catalog's own titles and sources are its owners' word.

version.description: Version of the requirements catalog. The requirements are versioned data, like the controls that satisfy them.

reviewedOn.description: Date the catalog was last reviewed, YYYY-MM-DD. A catalog nobody re-reads is a catalog the estate silently left behind.

owner.description: The team that owns the catalog. Requirements without an owner are promises nobody keeps.

requirements.description: The requirement rows: the obligations the estate must satisfy, each with its id, title, and source. An empty catalog claims the estate must satisfy nothing. The gate joins these ids against the controls manifest's mappings, in both directions.

id.description: The requirement's id (e.g. "PCI-DSS-2.2.7"). The controls map onto ids, and a row the join cannot cite is a row nobody satisfies.

title.description: What the requirement demands, in words an auditor can read.
